title: Vegetius battle-line reserve constructor with local failure repair
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Vegetius Epitoma rei militaris III.16–22 binds line spacing, centre wedge, cavalry wings, reserves behind the line, withdrawal and partial-flight responses. A persistent battle-line state lets a local flank pressure consume reserve or shorten the line without resetting the army; a catalogue rival misses the resource tradeoff.

source.work: Vegetius, Epitoma rei militaris, Book III
source.source_span: III.15–22 spacing, battle-line arrangement, reserves, commander positions, resistance, withdrawal and partial/whole flight
source_facts: The battle line has ordered spacing between men and ranks.
The centre can form a wedge; cavalry and light infantry protect or encircle wings.
Reserves are stationed behind the line; if one enemy mass presses a sector, removing troops to defend it strips another sector, while shortening the line and using reserves is advised.
Withdrawal and partial flight have separate responses.

duplicate_screen.checked: ideas search/duplicates Vegetius reserve/battle line and route-check transport/sequence/state; old transport cards excluded
duplicate_screen.difference: This is a local resource-preserving battle state with reserve consumption and partial-failure repair, not a cargo transport chain or generic event phase label.

worked_examples: PRESSURE(S0,left_wing)->THREAT(left); USE_RESERVE(S0,R,left)->S1 while right remains staffed
if no reserve, SHORTEN_LINE(S0)->S2; moving ordinary troops from right to left changes right-sector coverage
constructor.consequence: The same army identity survives a local threat, but choosing reserve use versus troop removal changes the unprotected sector and later battle state. A list rival predicts only that reserves exist and cannot distinguish local from whole-army flight.
constructor.smallest_test: Require two complete battle instructions with one shared deployment and opposite sector pressure, then test reserve use, line shortening, and partial-flight scope.
constructor.rival: Static inventory of formations where all mentioned troops remain available everywhere and order/sector consequences are ignored.
assumptions: Reserve and sector are typed state fields; no numeric troop count is invented.
The source's advice is normative military instruction, not a report of one battle.
failure_modes: The text is prescriptive and examples may not define one executable battle history.
No exact reserve size or timing is supplied.
A target could reuse a sequence marker for stylistic reasons without encoding resource state.

dependencies: No target military gloss or visual interpretation is made.
access: Source-only; no target, reserve, image, experiment, route, ledger, decoder, or root file access.
